reason: Final dependency and axiom-contract audit: Let C=<x> and L=<x^p>; the hypothesis implies x is p-singular and [C:L]=p. Write M as a summand of Ind_Q^H N. The integral Mackey formula restricts that induction to C as a finite sum of modules induced from C intersect conjugates of Q; none contains the p-part of x, so every such intersection lies in L. By induction transitivity, first induce each term to L, split it into indecomposable OL-lattices, and then induce to C. Green index-p indecomposability and Krull-Schmidt imply Res_C M is a sum of whole induced indecomposable terms. Frobenius' induced-character formula makes every such term vanish at x, since C is abelian and x is not in L. Hence theta(x)=0. AC is inherited exactly through the published relative-projectivity/Mackey contract; the local lattice decomposition and finite character calculation add no choice. This does not infer a summand's trace from cancellation in a larger induced module. Evidence inspected: Craven, The Brauer Correspondence, Theorem 2.20 and proof, pp. 28–29; Aschbacher–Kessar–Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Theorem 5.4 proof, pp. 276–277.
